message: OPERATOR DIRECTION — Do not escalate routine Git access as an architecture/permission decision. Agents already use Git regularly. Use the existing configured, authorized Git tooling, repository remotes, worktrees and credentials to perform the required READ-ONLY original-repository identity/ref/object verification directly, then continue eligible C0 work. First establish exactly what the requirement is (repository identity, commit/tree/parents, available refs) and run the minimal relevant Git read operations against the intended actual repository/host, documenting commands, target and verified outcomes. Distinguish normal repo access from genuinely unavailable *publisher-side original object custody*: do not assume a generic local clone or remote proves physical production publisher visibility. If the actual original Git objects cannot be verified with authorized facilities, report the exact command, target, failure and missing authority (rather than asking the Operator to design an implementation or make an A/B choice). Only ask for an Operator decision if there is an actual blocked privilege/action beyond existing authority. No new credentials, policy bypass, protected original ref writes, STOP changes, deploy, cutover or replay of uncertain external effects. Lead and Manager should dispatch already eligible unrelated work (especially Worker 6 independent Release proof) within verified capacity; do not hold runnable work behind C0. Respond via Operator notification with concrete evidence and results, not another abstract escalation.
